previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to diarrhea and redness in her left arm one week after AV loop graft placement. Evaluation revealed cellulitis at the graft site and overflow diarrhea from opioid-induced constipation. She was treated with IV vancomycin, transitioned to oral doxycycline, and underwent two hemodialysis sessions. Her infection improved, white count normalized, and bowel symptoms resolved with a bowel regimen. Transplant surgery evaluated her for possible steal syndrome, recommending outpatient follow-up for potential graft ligation. She was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, avoid opioids, monitor graft site, and attend follow-up appointments.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___, 

Thank you for allowing us to participate in your care at ___. 
You were admitted to the hospital because of diabetic 
ketoacidosis and injury to your heart muscle. You were evaluated 
by our endocrinologists who adjusted your insulin regimen. It is 
important that you take your insulin as prescribed in order to 
prevent further episodes of DKA, which can be life threatening. 

While in the hospital, you were found to have injury to your 
heart muscle. We evaluated you with a stress test which showed 
some evidence of injury to your heart. We evaluated you with a 
cardiac catheterization which showed blockages in the arteries 
that supply your heart. We put a stent in one of those arteries 
to help keep it open. You may need an additional cardiac 
catheterization in the future to open up some of the other 
arteries.  After discharge please weigh yourself every morning, 
call your doctor if your weight goes up more than 3 lbs.

After your catheterization, we found there was a small 
connection between the arteries and the veins in your leg called 
a fistula. You were evaluated by the vascular surgeons who felt 
this fistula was small and was not causing any problems to the 
blood flow in your leg and did not require any further 
intervention. 

While in the hospital you were found to have an infection of 
your right index finger. You were evaluated by hand surgery. An 
x-ray did not suggest infection in your bone. We treated you 
with antibiotics (called Doxycycline), which you should continue 
through ___.
